speaker: Doctor
text:
Good morning, I see you have a history of a painful, swollen left ankle that resolved on its own, and now you are experiencing increasing pain and swelling in your right knee along with episodes of pain during urination. To understand the connection between these symptoms, have you noticed any redness or warmth in the affected joints?

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis
REQUEST TEST: Inflammatory_Markers

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Protein Negative, Blood Negative, WBC 12–16/hpf, RBC 1–2/hpf; Inflammatory Markers: Erythrocyte_Sedimentation_Rate 38 mm/h

speaker: Doctor
text:
The urinalysis indicates white blood cells in the urine, and your elevated ESR suggests active inflammation, which aligns with your history of a self-resolving ankle joint issue. Given the pattern of recurrent, asymmetric joint involvement and sterile-looking inflammation, are you currently experiencing a fever or chills?

REQUEST TEST: Joint_aspiration_right_knee
REQUEST IMAGES: Knee_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Arthrocentesis of Right Knee: Appearance of Synovial Fluid Cloudy, Gram Stain Negative, Leukocyte Count in Synovial Fluid 26,000/mm3, Percent Neutrophils 75%; Knee_X-Ray: Not Provided in Available Data

speaker: Doctor
text: The synovial fluid shows high neutrophil count with a negative Gram stain, and your urine has white blood cells, which rules out septic arthritis but points to an inflammatory cause. Given your history of a self-resolving ankle attack and current knee findings, have you experienced any sudden, severe pain in your eye or noticed eye redness in the past?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive arthritis (formerly Reiter's syndrome). The combination of asymmetric oligoarthritis (ankle, now knee), urethritis (painful urination), conjunctivitis risk, and a history of inconsistent condom use strongly supports this diagnosis.
